refutation.quote: So on hard problems the 8 directions are more than the cue (answers the check on result-36e8cd), they are direction-specific, and they cut cap hits
refutation.note: result-284db5 (after cutoff, hard328, cue, T 1.0): cued base 164 vs cued base + Math top-8 192 (paired +8.5 [4.3, 12.8]). Cap hits fall 77 -> 46, Wait rises to RL's level (9.2 -> 12.3 per 1,000 words, RL 12.9), and top-8 solves 30 of the 49 problems only RL solved. The theory's core claim is that top8 is the cue 'and nothing more', so top8 and the cue should not add up. Here top8 adds clearly on top of the cue, and with RL-type checking. The scope names hard328 as excluded ('where RL's long checking may matter more'), so formally this is out of scope. But the advocate still made a held-out claim on this cell (t45: 168, which is cued-base level) and lost -3.0 against measured 192. The in-scope offline numbers lean the same way: quick finished-wrongs 22 (above the theory's interval 5-21 and above the cued base's own 13), and length ratio 0.25 (near the top of the interval, toward RL). Also read: result-dc15a1, where a hand-written cue edit scores 85 vs top8 88 and prefilled cue 82 on the first 100, which supports the theory's MATH-500 claim; result-ad3c24, result-36e8cd and result-d2933e (top8 427, random 197, bulk 91).

wins_judgement: The offline total of +1.856 rests on one test. p2 (quick finished-wrong count) gives +1.89 although the measured 22 fell outside the theory's interval [5, 21]. It scores because both no-theory readers put their centres lower (8, 9). The mechanism does not earn this: it predicted the cued base's count (~13, said as 11), and the measured value is well above that. That excess is what the rival's plain-register mixture predicts. p1 (median log length ratio 0.25 vs predicted 0.12) gains only +0.008: any reader guessing 'somewhat longer than the cued base' gets the same. p3 (overlap 0.356, at the theory's lower edge) loses -0.04. Held-out t45 loses -3.0. The test script tests/r5-m03/p2.py implements the recipe as written: it keeps score_v3 == 0, cap_hit False and n_generated <= 2000, dedups problem_index, and skips missing score_v3. So the one positive gain is real arithmetic but does not support the mechanism.
rival: The rival explains the numbers better. In the duel the state is 'loses to rival', total -8.767, and all 3 tests separate the two and favour the rival. The rival says top8 is a sample-by-sample mixture: about 85-90 % of answers are RL-like and the rest are plain-base register. (1) Of top8's wrong problems, 0.25 are ones the cued base solves 4/4 (theory 0.13 [0.06, 0.22], rival 0.27); gain -2.77. (2) On top8's quick wrongs the mean cued-base solve rate is 0.818 (theory 0.5 [0.3, 0.7], rival 0.76); gain -3.0. (3) The share of quick wrongs at <= 1,000 tokens is 0.773 (theory 0.4, rival 0.63); about -3. These show that top8's quick errors fall on problems the cued base finds easy and are very short. That is plain-base behaviour, not cued-base slips. I read rivals/r5-m03/p2.py: it implements the rival recipe as written (attempt == 0 rows, k/m per problem, m == 0 dropped, each problem once). The rival also accounts for the 22 quick wrongs, the length ratio of 0.25 between T1 and RL, the overlap of 0.356, and result-284db5. The deciding target not yet run is the theory's own GPU cell, top8 + cue on MATH-500 (theory ~425, refuted at >= 441). Test 2 separates the two most sharply among the tests already run.

novelty.nearest: Cai et al., 'On Predictability of RL Dynamics for LLMs' (Rank-1 Dominance): the top singular subspace of the RL weight update, added to the base, recovers >99 % of RL's reasoning gains. Related: 2509.06608 (RL steering vector acts as a first-token substitution bias, and a 'To' prefix gives ~75 %) and 2610.24663 (forcing the RL opening 'Alright' recovers 35 % of the gain, later RL choices more).
novelty.difference: The paper shows that a low-rank RL update recovers the gains but does not say what behaviour it carries. The theory adds that the top-8 directions carry only the opening register (equivalent to the text cue, non-additive with it), not RL's checking or length.

import_carries_gain.which: The import 2509.06608 ('a low-rank RL component equals a text prefix, so edit and cue do not add up') directly drives the held-out t45 claim (top8 + cue at cued-base level, 168) and the GPU top8+cue prediction. t45 lost -3.0 (measured 192). The only positive gain, p2, came from the readers' low intervals, not from the prefix-equivalence import, and the measured value overshot the import-derived cued-base level.

verdict: weak: duel state 'loses to rival' (-8.77, all 3 tests favour the rival's mixture account); its only offline gain rests on one test whose value fell outside its interval; and result-284db5 (top8 adds +8.5 on top of the cue, with RL-level Wait rates) contradicts its 'nothing more than the cue' core, although hard328 is formally outside its scope.
